sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Apply directly to PhD if that is your aim, including without a master’s; funded applicants can earn the master’s
en route. Program table lists GPA 3.0. UChicago bachelor’s plus appropriate preparation is an eligible route;
international applications are accepted. [s1] [s2] [s4] [s6]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Prepare transcripts, 2-3-page personal statement and three referees; choose PhD for assistantship
consideration. If seeking the departmental fee waiver, submit the complete unpaid application by January 16
and email Laura Anderson a justification. Financial documents may wait until after admission. [s2] [s4] [s5]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No supervisor agreement required. Faculty below are research-fit contacts; Huy Dang is a visiting assistant
professor and should not be treated as a permanent primary adviser without confirmation. [s1] [s9] [s15]
Portal workflow [Unresolved]
Not established by the cited public admissions materials. Confirm in the current application or with graduate
admissions before relying on a rule.
Cycle verification [2027 confirmed]
Deadlines are standing. Funding base is explicitly announced for 2027-28 and independently corroborated by
university news. [s1] [s7] [s17]

sections.title: Deadlines by stage
sections.text:
Academic application [Standing rule]
Fall: April 15 for full admission consideration; January 30 for funding. Spring table lists November 30, but
confirm funded PhD spring availability. Dates are recurring, no time zone. April 15 here is an APPLICATION
date, not an offer-acceptance deadline. [s1] [s2]
Funding consideration; Reference receipt; Supporting documents [Standing rule]
Submit all materials by January 30 for funding; letters should arrive before the program deadline. General final
admission consideration April 15. Fee-waiver applicants seeking funding must submit complete unpaid file by
January 16. No separate referee grace period is published. [s1] [s3] [s5]
Test-score receipt [Standing rule]
Official scores, where required, should reach Graduate Admissions by the relevant program deadline. Testing
agency delivery can take two full weeks. GRE is not required. [s2] [s3]

Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
Not established by the cited public admissions materials. Confirm in the current application or with graduate
admissions before relying on a rule.

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Standing rule]
Central guidelines include TOEFL 80 on the old scale, PTE 53 and Duolingo 105; submit official electronic
reports to Graduate Admissions, not mathematics. Revised TOEFL scale and IELTS threshold should be
confirmed on the current page if testing is needed. [s4]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Expected or completed bachelor’s from the U.S. qualifies by enrollment. Applicants not yet eligible may apply
without scores and receive provisional admission until the waiver is verified; provisional status cannot support
I-20/DS-2019 issuance. Contact gradadmission@binghamton.edu to confirm. Two years of eligible full-time
English-medium study provides another route. [s4]
GRE General; GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Program table says GRE not required without distinguishing General/Subject. Optional-score consideration and
permission are not explicitly specified. [s2]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three letters for Mathematical Sciences (overrides central general two-letter minimum). [s2] [s3]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
Department lists Squier assistantships, research fellowships and occasional summer support. Kappe is
described as for a U.S. student, with SUNY preference; eligibility of an F-1 UChicago student is not established
and should not be assumed. Extra scholarship essays/references are not public in the mathematics checklist.
[s5] [s6]
What sends the invitation [Standing rule]
Submitting referee contact information triggers emailed upload instructions, before final application
submission if entered earlier. [s3]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
You may submit the application before letters arrive; continued access to referee list allows reminders or
recommender changes. This does not extend the letter deadline. [s3]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
An email confirmation is sent to the applicant when the referee uploads a letter. [s3]

Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
Recommenders can be changed and reminded after submission. Public guidance does not establish
replacement of an already filed letter or reuse across applications/cycles. [s3]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [2027 confirmed]
Central policy explicitly announces USD 27,500 for AY 2027-28, ten months, as base stipend for in-person
doctoral programs normally providing full GA/TA funding. Mathematics offers full tuition with assistantships.
Full-time PhDs receive broad-based-fee scholarships, excluding international student fees; offer controls
individual eligibility. A USD 750 doctoral transition award is announced for eligible entering assistantship
holders. [s5] [s6] [s7] [s17]
Years of support; Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Department renews after year one subject to satisfactory academic/assistantship work; more rigorous review
after year two. Continued successful students can generally expect support through PhD, subject to six-year
Graduate School cap. Legally awards are one year at a time. Some summer support exists, not guaranteed. [s6]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International application guidance says candidates are evaluated for assistantships on merit; funding
information is not shared with admission committee. International student fees remain outside the
broad-based-fee scholarship. [s4] [s5]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
All applicants are considered for assistantships; no separate application form or extra materials unless the
program specifies them. Apply to PhD and meet January 30. [s4] [s6] [s8]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Department lists Squier assistantships, research fellowships and occasional summer support. Kappe is
described as for a U.S. student, with SUNY preference; eligibility of an F-1 UChicago student is not established
and should not be assumed. Extra scholarship essays/references are not public in the mathematics checklist.
[s5] [s6]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 75, nonrefundable; payment or approved waiver is necessary for review. [s3] [s5]

Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Limited mathematics PhD waivers: submit every required item but do NOT pay, then email
landersn@binghamton.edu with justification. For funding, submit by January 16 (two weeks before January 30);
decision arrives about one week before deadline. If denied, pay before deadline. No citizenship restriction
stated for this departmental route. [s5]

Department funding page says student fees are not included, whereas newer central program information
provides broad-based-fee scholarships for full-time PhDs but excludes international fees. Preserve both and
obtain itemized offer. [s5] [s6]

sections.title: Potential advisers and recent research
sections.text:
Algebraic / arithmetic geometry
Alexander Borisov
Birational/toric geometry, polynomial morphisms and arithmetic questions. [s9] [s10] [s11]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2026 manuscript (with Ofer Gabber and Adrian Vasiu) · On endomorphisms of affine spaces and the
Jacobian problem
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Adrian Vasiu
Shimura varieties, abelian/group schemes, Galois representations and arithmetic differential geometry. [s9]
[s11]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2026 book · Delta-invariant theory for Hecke correspondences
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Pratik Misra
Algebraic statistics and graphical models: an applied-algebraic-geometry fit rather than classical/arithmetic
geometry. [s9] [s13] [s14]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2026 · Coloured Gaussian directed acyclic graphical models
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Huy Dang
Wild ramification, Galois covers of curves in characteristic p, deformation/lifting. [s15]
Visiting assistant professor; primary PhD supervision availability not established.
Research evidence: 2026 · a-Numbers of cyclic degree p² covers of the projective line
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.

Number theory
Marcin Mazur
Group schemes, integral group rings, Galois modules and Galois representations. Recent paper not verified on
the official profile/homepage. [s9] [s12] [s16] [q18]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2006 · On mod p logarithms log_a b and log_b a
University-hosted historical paper; a recent publication was not established after checking the institutional profile, author page
and targeted publication searches. Current projects need confirmation.

United States · Mathematical Sciences PhD
Roster and rank verification handled separately
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• January 16 is the fee-waiver preparation deadline for funded applications.
• April 15 is an application deadline here.
• English provisional admission blocks I-20 issuance until waiver or test verification.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Apply directly to PhD if that is your aim, including without a master’s; funded applicants can earn the master’s
en route. Program table lists GPA 3.0. UChicago bachelor’s plus appropriate preparation is an eligible route;
international applications are accepted. [s1] [s2] [s4] [s6]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Prepare transcripts, 2-3-page personal statement and three referees; choose PhD for assistantship
consideration. If seeking the departmental fee waiver, submit the complete unpaid application by January 16
and email Laura Anderson a justification. Financial documents may wait until after admission. [s2] [s4] [s5]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No supervisor agreement required. Faculty below are research-fit contacts; Huy Dang is a visiting assistant
professor and should not be treated as a permanent primary adviser without confirmation. [s1] [s9] [s15]
Portal workflow [Unresolved]
Not established by the cited public admissions materials. Confirm in the current application or with graduate
admissions before relying on a rule.
Cycle verification [2027 confirmed]
Deadlines are standing. Funding base is explicitly announced for 2027-28 and independently corroborated by
university news. [s1] [s7] [s17]
Deadlines by stage
Academic application [Standing rule]
Fall: April 15 for full admission consideration; January 30 for funding. Spring table lists November 30, but
confirm funded PhD spring availability. Dates are recurring, no time zone. April 15 here is an APPLICATION
date, not an offer-acceptance deadline. [s1] [s2]
Funding consideration; Reference receipt; Supporting documents [Standing rule]
Submit all materials by January 30 for funding; letters should arrive before the program deadline. General final
admission consideration April 15. Fee-waiver applicants seeking funding must submit complete unpaid file by
January 16. No separate referee grace period is published. [s1] [s3] [s5]
Test-score receipt [Standing rule]
Official scores, where required, should reach Graduate Admissions by the relevant program deadline. Testing
agency delivery can take two full weeks. GRE is not required. [s2] [s3]

Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
Not established by the cited public admissions materials. Confirm in the current application or with graduate
admissions before relying on a rule.
English and GRE
English requirement [Standing rule]
Central guidelines include TOEFL 80 on the old scale, PTE 53 and Duolingo 105; submit official electronic
reports to Graduate Admissions, not mathematics. Revised TOEFL scale and IELTS threshold should be
confirmed on the current page if testing is needed. [s4]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Expected or completed bachelor’s from the U.S. qualifies by enrollment. Applicants not yet eligible may apply
without scores and receive provisional admission until the waiver is verified; provisional status cannot support
I-20/DS-2019 issuance. Contact gradadmission@binghamton.edu to confirm. Two years of eligible full-time
English-medium study provides another route. [s4]
GRE General; GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Program table says GRE not required without distinguishing General/Subject. Optional-score consideration and
permission are not explicitly specified. [s2]
Academic records
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Graduate application requires academic transcripts; exact current upload/consolidation and final
official-conferral instructions should be checked in the application-materials page/portal. Do not omit
institutions because a transfer credit appears elsewhere. [s3]
Mathematics-course list; Course descriptions [Standing rule]
Not listed as a separate required item on the public mathematics application checklist. This does not establish
whether the current portal permits an optional upload; exact prompt, length, formatting and upload/link rule
are not published. [s2]
Recommendation letters
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three letters for Mathematical Sciences (overrides central general two-letter minimum). [s2] [s3]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
Department lists Squier assistantships, research fellowships and occasional summer support. Kappe is
described as for a U.S. student, with SUNY preference; eligibility of an F-1 UChicago student is not established
and should not be assumed. Extra scholarship essays/references are not public in the mathematics checklist.
[s5] [s6]
What sends the invitation [Standing rule]
Submitting referee contact information triggers emailed upload instructions, before final application
submission if entered earlier. [s3]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
You may submit the application before letters arrive; continued access to referee list allows reminders or
recommender changes. This does not extend the letter deadline. [s3]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
An email confirmation is sent to the applicant when the referee uploads a letter. [s3]

Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
Recommenders can be changed and reminded after submission. Public guidance does not establish
replacement of an already filed letter or reuse across applications/cycles. [s3]
Written materials
Academic CV / resume; Research proposal; Writing sample / thesis / research summary;
Publications list; Course-list document; Other short answers / materials [Standing rule]
Not listed as a separate required item on the public mathematics application checklist. This does not establish
whether the current portal permits an optional upload; exact prompt, length, formatting and upload/link rule
are not published. [s2]
Statement of purpose; Personal / background statement; Research-interest statement [Standing
rule]
Required personal statement, 2-3 pages. Short public prompt: describe interest in graduate study and career
aspirations. Font, spacing, file format and whether supplementary links are allowed are not specified. No
separate SOP or research-interest statement is identified. [s2]
Scholarship essays [Standing rule]
Department lists Squier assistantships, research fellowships and occasional summer support. Kappe is
described as for a U.S. student, with SUNY preference; eligibility of an F-1 UChicago student is not established
and should not be assumed. Extra scholarship essays/references are not public in the mathematics checklist.
[s5] [s6]
Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [2027 confirmed]
Central policy explicitly announces USD 27,500 for AY 2027-28, ten months, as base stipend for in-person
doctoral programs normally providing full GA/TA funding. Mathematics offers full tuition with assistantships.
Full-time PhDs receive broad-based-fee scholarships, excluding international student fees; offer controls
individual eligibility. A USD 750 doctoral transition award is announced for eligible entering assistantship
holders. [s5] [s6] [s7] [s17]
Years of support; Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Department renews after year one subject to satisfactory academic/assistantship work; more rigorous review
after year two. Continued successful students can generally expect support through PhD, subject to six-year
Graduate School cap. Legally awards are one year at a time. Some summer support exists, not guaranteed. [s6]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International application guidance says candidates are evaluated for assistantships on merit; funding
information is not shared with admission committee. International student fees remain outside the
broad-based-fee scholarship. [s4] [s5]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
All applicants are considered for assistantships; no separate application form or extra materials unless the
program specifies them. Apply to PhD and meet January 30. [s4] [s6] [s8]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Department lists Squier assistantships, research fellowships and occasional summer support. Kappe is
described as for a U.S. student, with SUNY preference; eligibility of an F-1 UChicago student is not established
and should not be assumed. Extra scholarship essays/references are not public in the mathematics checklist.
[s5] [s6]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 75, nonrefundable; payment or approved waiver is necessary for review. [s3] [s5]

Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Limited mathematics PhD waivers: submit every required item but do NOT pay, then email
landersn@binghamton.edu with justification. For funding, submit by January 16 (two weeks before January 30);
decision arrives about one week before deadline. If denied, pay before deadline. No citizenship restriction
stated for this departmental route. [s5]
Conflicts and remaining checks
Conflicting sources [Conflict]
Department funding page says student fees are not included, whereas newer central program information
provides broad-based-fee scholarships for full-time PhDs but excludes international fees. Preserve both and
obtain itemized offer. [s5] [s6]
Checks still needed [Unresolved]
Confirm deadline time zone, official-transcript deadline, current English-score table if needed, waiver
verification timing, TA language screening/insurance, commitment date, scholarship prompts and letter
reuse/replacement. Mazur’s recent paper metadata is not public on the reviewed profile/homepage. [s1] [s3] [s4]

Algebraic / arithmetic geometry
Alexander Borisov
Birational/toric geometry, polynomial morphisms and arithmetic questions. [s9] [s10] [s11]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2026 manuscript (with Ofer Gabber and Adrian Vasiu) · On endomorphisms of affine spaces and the
Jacobian problem
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Adrian Vasiu
Shimura varieties, abelian/group schemes, Galois representations and arithmetic differential geometry. [s9]
[s11]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2026 book · Delta-invariant theory for Hecke correspondences
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Pratik Misra
Algebraic statistics and graphical models: an applied-algebraic-geometry fit rather than classical/arithmetic
geometry. [s9] [s13] [s14]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2026 · Coloured Gaussian directed acyclic graphical models
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Huy Dang
Wild ramification, Galois covers of curves in characteristic p, deformation/lifting. [s15]
Visiting assistant professor; primary PhD supervision availability not established.
Research evidence: 2026 · a-Numbers of cyclic degree p² covers of the projective line
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
